subject: Log scale, linear labels in geom_crossbar

messages.author: 519455d3bf64680d
messages.subject: Log scale, linear labels in geom_crossbar
parts:
I am displaying the results of logistic regression analyses (as
odds-ratios) using crossbar... it is a nice way to tell stories to lay
audiences. However, I want the Y axis to be base e, so that odds ratios
above and below 1 have similar visual impact. However, I need the
metrification of the axis to be in base 10, not e. When I used
scale_y_continuous(transform="log") I get e scaling and notation on the
axis.

I poked around looking for the various options that the option FORMATTER
might provide, but did not find an exhaustive list. Perhaps the answer
is there.

Again, many thanks.

Rob

messages.subject: Re: Log scale, linear labels in geom_crossbar
parts:
Thanks Charlotte,

Both transform="log" and transform="log10" produce an exponentiated
scale e ^1, e^-1, (as superscripts) or 10^1, 10^0.5, etc , 10^-1, etc.
Which is all fine and good for some audiences, but for other audience,
they'd much prefer to have their label unexponentiated.. So, what I
need are base 10 integers and reals to annotate the label:e.g.
1,2,3,5,10, 0.5, 0.3, 0.1, etc.


That's what I meant to say.

Thanks as always!

messages.author: 70ab9fabb9f066d8
messages.subject: Re: Log scale, linear labels in geom_crossbar
parts:
Ah I see. I think I've always dealt with this by manually specifying
the breaks and labels.

df <- data.frame(x = rnorm(10), y = 10^rnorm(10))
qplot(x,y, data = df) + scale_y_continuous(trans = "log10", breaks =
10^seq(-4, 4, 1), labels = 10^seq(-4, 4, 1))

Charlotte
